gloss: easy to imagine / not hard to
pat: Noun / V dict + に難くない
x: 〜に難くない is a literary construction meaning 'not hard to X' — typically used with verbs of imagination, understanding, or inference to indicate that the main clause situation is readily graspable. Common fixed forms: 想像に難くない ('easy to imagine'), 察するに難くない ('easy to infer'). Very formal / literary register.
notes: Literary / formal 'not hard to X'.
Most common fixed form: 想像に難くない ('easy to imagine').
j: 彼の苦労は想像に難くない。
e: His hardship is easy to imagine.

gloss: will not fail to / will inevitably
pat: V ない-form + ではおかない
x: 〜ないではおかない is a less literary variant of 〜ずにはおかない, expressing determined action or natural inevitability — 'will not leave without X happening'. Formal register, interchangeable in meaning with ずにはおかない. The form uses the casual negative ない-form with ではおかない.
notes: Less formal variant of 〜ずにはおかない — same two senses (resolve / inevitability).
The negative form attaches directly: 言わない → 言わないではおかない.
j: 彼に一言言わないではおかない。
e: I will not leave without saying a word to him.
_k: 書かないではおかない

gloss: (I'll) just / I'll simply X (if needed)
pat: V dict-form + までだ / までのことだ
x: 〜までだ / 〜までのことだ expresses a speaker's resolve to take a specific (often unremarkable or last-resort) action if necessary — 'I'll just X'. The main clause action is presented as a simple, unchallenging fallback. Formal register, common in declarations of resolve.
notes: Resolved fallback — 'in that case, I'll simply X'.
Two variants: までだ (shorter) and までのことだ (slightly more emphatic).
j: だめなら、諦めるまでだ。
e: If it doesn't work, I'll just give up.

gloss: all I did was / it was simply because
pat: V-た form + までのことだ
x: 〜たまでのことだ downplays an action as unremarkable or modest — 'all I did was X' / 'I was simply doing X'. Common in humble responses to praise or explanations of a small action. Distinct from the V-dict form までだ which expresses future resolve.
notes: Modest / downplaying — 'I was just doing X, nothing special'.
Common in humble responses: 礼なんて、当然のことをしたまでのことだ ('you don't need to thank me — I just did what was natural').
j: お礼を言われることではない。当然のことをしたまでのことです。
e: No need to thank me — I just did what was natural.

gloss: to think that / I didn't expect that / the fact that
x: 〜とは expresses surprise, amazement, or disbelief at a fact — 'to think that X!' / 'I didn't expect that X'. Often used in exclamations of surprise. Can also introduce a definition: '〜とは (the term) X means'. Two related but distinct uses; context disambiguates.
notes: Surprise / disbelief: 彼が来るとは、思わなかった ('I didn't think he'd come').
Definition: 友情とは、助け合うことだ ('friendship means helping each other').
j: 彼が来るとは思わなかった。
e: I never thought he'd come.

gloss: without doing / without even
x: 〜ことなしに is a formal / literary construction meaning 'without doing X' — the Y clause is achieved or attempted without X having occurred. More formal than 〜ずに or 〜ないで. Often used in declarative statements where X would normally be expected.
notes: Formal / literary 'without X'.
More formal than 〜ずに (formal) and 〜ないで (neutral).
j: 努力することなしに、成功はあり得ない。
e: Without making an effort, success is impossible.

gloss: when one becomes / when it comes to being
pat: Noun / V plain + ともなれば
x: 〜ともなれば expresses 'when one is / becomes X' — emphasizing the natural consequences of reaching or being in a specific role or state. The main clause typically describes the responsibilities or expectations that naturally follow. Formal / literary register. Distinct from 〜となれば (more circumstantial).
notes: Role / state consequences — 'once one is X, then naturally Y'.
Similar to 〜となれば (N3) but more about status / role than circumstance.
j: 大人ともなれば、責任を持たなければならない。
e: Once one is an adult, one must bear responsibility.

gloss: while also / alongside (doing)
pat: V plain / noun + の + かたわら
x: 〜かたわら expresses that the subject does a secondary activity alongside the main one — 'while also doing X'. Typically for two long-term ongoing activities (e.g., work and study). Formal / literary register. Different from 〜ながら (simultaneous single-action) in that かたわら is for parallel long-term roles.
notes: Parallel long-term activities — not simultaneous single actions.
Common: 仕事のかたわら, 勉強のかたわら, 子育てのかたわら.
j: 彼は会社で働くかたわら、夜は大学で学んでいる。
e: He works at a company, while also studying at university at night.

gloss: must not / should not (archaic prohibition)
pat: V dict-form + べからず / べからざる
x: 〜べからず is an archaic / classical prohibition meaning 'must not X'. Rare in modern speech, common in old signs and proverbs. The attributive form べからざる is used as a modifier — 'that must not be Xed'. Fixed form: 〜べからざる+ 行為 ('an act that must not be done').
notes: Archaic prohibition — very rare in modern speech.
Common in historical signs: 立ち入るべからず ('no entry').
j: ここに立ち入るべからず。
e: No entry here.

gloss: can't get by without / must inevitably do
pat: V negative stem + ずにはすまない / ないではすまない
x: 〜ずにはすまない expresses that the speaker cannot let X go undone — 'one cannot get by without doing X' / 'X must inevitably happen'. Often used for obligations arising from social or moral pressure. Formal register. Irregular: する → せずにはすまない.
notes: Social / moral inevitability — one cannot escape doing X.
Irregular: せずにはすまない for する.
j: 謝らずにはすまないだろう。
e: He'll have no choice but to apologize.

gloss: can't (do X) even if one wanted to
pat: V volitional + にも + V potential negative
x: 〜ようにも〜ない expresses that an action is impossible even though the subject would like to do it — 'I can't do X even if I wanted to'. The X verb appears twice: once in volitional form + にも, then in potential negative. Literary / formal register.
notes: Double-verb structure — the same verb appears in volitional + にも and potential negative.
Literary register — common in narratives of frustrated action.
j: 言おうにも言えない状況だ。
e: It's a situation where I can't speak even if I wanted to.

gloss: in order to / for the purpose of (literary)
pat: V ない-stem + んがため(に)
x: 〜んがため(に) is a literary / archaic purpose marker meaning 'in order to X'. More formal and older-sounding than 〜ために or 〜ように. Rare in modern speech, common in essays, historical writing, and formal prose. Irregular: する → せんがため.
notes: Very literary / archaic purpose marker.
Irregular: せんがため for する.
j: 真実を知らんがために、調査を続けた。
e: In order to know the truth, he continued the investigation.

gloss: as if about to / looking as if
pat: V ない-stem + んばかり(に)
x: 〜んばかり(に) expresses that something looks as if it is about to happen or happen intensely — 'as if about to X'. Often used metaphorically for emphasis: 泣かんばかりに ('as if about to cry'). Literary register. The ん is from archaic negative む, but the meaning is 'about to'.
notes: Metaphorical 'as if about to' — often hyperbolic.
Common: 泣かんばかりに, 飛びかからんばかりに, 叫ばんばかりに.
j: 彼女は泣かんばかりの表情だった。
e: She had an expression as if she were about to cry.

gloss: at the moment of / as soon as (literary)
pat: Verb dict-form + や / や否や
x: 〜や / 〜や否や is a literary / classical 'as soon as' construction. Very dramatic in tone, common in classical prose and formal narratives. Similar in meaning to 〜なり (N2 literary 'as soon as') and 〜たとたん (N3). Verb stays in dictionary form.
notes: Literary / classical 'as soon as'.
や alone or や否や (same meaning).
j: 彼は家を出るや、走り出した。
e: The moment he left the house, he ran off.

gloss: in view of / out of consideration for / for the sake of appearance
pat: V plain / noun + の + 手前
x: 〜手前 expresses that an action is taken out of consideration for something or someone — often 'out of face' or 'in view of X'. The speaker feels obliged to act a certain way because of social appearance or previous commitments. Formal / literary register.
notes: Social / face-saving consideration — 'out of consideration for X'.
Often when the speaker must act a certain way for appearances.
j: 約束した手前、引き下がれない。
e: Having promised, I can't back down.

gloss: (although) at / while / in the middle of (polite apology)
pat: V plain / adj + ところを
x: 〜ところを is a polite / formal construction used when interrupting or apologizing for taking someone's time — 'while X (I apologize for disturbing)'. Common in business and formal speech, especially in the phrase お忙しいところを ('while you're busy'). Formal register.
notes: Polite apology for interrupting — formal business register.
Common fixed phrase: お忙しいところを (apologizing for taking busy time).
j: お忙しいところを、ありがとうございます。
e: Thank you for your time despite being busy.

gloss: does not hesitate to / declares openly
pat: V-て form + はばからない
x: 〜てはばからない expresses that the subject does something without hesitation or inhibition — 'does X openly / unapologetically'. Often with assertions, declarations, or bold actions. Usually with a note of surprise or criticism from the speaker at the directness. Literary / formal register.
notes: 'Doesn't hold back' — often implies directness that surprises or criticizes.
Common with verbs of speaking: 言ってはばからない, 主張してはばからない.
j: 彼は自分が一番だと言ってはばからない。
e: He openly declares he's the best.

gloss: no way to / cannot possibly
x: 〜べくもない expresses that something is impossible — 'there is no way to X'. Built on the classical べし ('should / must') with negation. More literary / emphatic than 〜ようがない. Rare in modern casual speech, common in literary and formal writing.
notes: Literary 'no way to / cannot possibly'.
Related to 〜べき / 〜べからず via the classical べし.
j: 彼の意図を知るべくもない。
e: There's no way to know his intentions.

gloss: some kind of / (I hear) something like
x: 〜とやら expresses that the speaker is uncertain about the exact detail — 'some kind of X' / 'something called X'. The speaker has heard of X but is hazy on specifics. Common in conversation when referring to things secondhand. Formal / literary register.
notes: Vagueness / secondhand knowledge — the speaker doesn't fully know.
Common when referring to things by name without commitment: 田中さんとやら ('someone named Tanaka').
j: 田中さんとやらは、どこの人ですか。
e: This Tanaka person — where is he from?

gloss: on the occasion of / when
pat: V plain / noun + の + 折(に)
x: 〜折(に) is a formal / polite temporal marker meaning 'on the occasion of' — a specific moment or opportunity. More formal than 〜とき, often used in polite correspondence and formal speech. Common in set phrases and polite framings.
notes: Formal 'on the occasion of' — more polite than とき or 際.
Common in polite correspondence: お近くにお越しの折には ('when you come near us').
j: お近くにお越しの折には、お寄りください。
e: When you come near us, please drop by.

gloss: while / in (the state of) / from the start
pat: Noun / V stem + ながらに(して)
x: 〜ながらに is a literary construction expressing that the main action is done 'while in the state of X' or 'in a way that preserves X'. Often with 生まれ (born), 涙 (tears), 昔 (the past): 生まれながらに ('since birth'), 涙ながらに ('tearfully'), 昔ながらに ('as in the old days'). Distinct from 〜ながら (simultaneous single-action).
notes: Literary 'while in / from' — state-preserving.
Common fixed forms: 生まれながらに, 涙ながらに, 昔ながらに, 居ながらにして.
j: 彼は生まれながらにして、才能があった。
e: He had talent from birth.

gloss: succeed in completing / manage to do fully
pat: Verb ます-stem + おおせる
x: 〜おおせる is a literary auxiliary meaning 'succeed in completing X' — the subject managed to do X fully, often despite difficulty or being under pressure. Carries a note of accomplishment. Common with verbs of accomplishment, deception, and task completion. Literary register.
notes: Literary auxiliary — 'succeed in fully doing X'.
Often with difficult or secretive actions: 逃げおおせる ('succeed in escaping'), 言いおおせる ('manage to say'), やりおおせる ('manage to accomplish').
j: 犯人は警察から逃げおおせた。
e: The criminal succeeded in escaping the police.

gloss: handle skillfully / master / do expertly
x: 〜こなす is an auxiliary expressing that the subject handles an action skillfully or masterfully — 'do X expertly'. Often with language, technology, or complex tasks: 使いこなす ('master the use of'), 乗りこなす ('ride skillfully'), 着こなす ('wear stylishly'). Neutral / formal register.
notes: Skillful mastery — 'handle X expertly'.
Common: 使いこなす (master using), 乗りこなす (ride well), 着こなす (wear stylishly).
j: 彼は英語を使いこなしている。
e: He has mastered the use of English.

gloss: without even needing to / not even requiring
x: 〜までもなく expresses that something was achieved or concluded without needing to go so far as to do X — 'without even needing X'. Often a shortened form of 〜までもない ('no need to even'). Used to show that a result was reached easily or that a step was unnecessary. Formal register.
notes: Related to 〜までもない (no need to even).
The adverbial form until (-naku) modifies the main clause — 'without even requiring X'.
j: 言うまでもなく、彼は天才だ。
e: Needless to say, he is a genius.

gloss: if it were at least X (that would be OK, but)
pat: Noun / plain form + ならまだしも
x: 〜ならまだしも expresses that while X would be acceptable or tolerable, the actual situation (Y, described in the main clause) goes beyond what is OK — 'if only X, that would be fine, but Y is too much'. Used to escalate criticism or complaint by comparison.
notes: Escalating criticism — 'X would be OK, but Y crosses the line'.
Common in complaints and disappointment: 一度ならまだしも、何度もは困る ('once would be OK, but many times is a problem').
j: 一度ならまだしも、何度も遅刻するのは困る。
e: Once I could accept, but being late repeatedly is a problem.

gloss: if it were X, I wouldn't know / X might be one thing but
pat: Noun / plain form + ならいざ知らず
x: 〜ならいざ知らず expresses that while X might be a legitimate exception, Y (the main clause situation) is definitely not — 'X might be understandable, but Y isn't'. Similar in function to 〜ならまだしも but with a slightly more dismissive / exceptional framing. Literary / formal register.
notes: Contrastive exception — 'X might be a case where I couldn't say, but Y is clearly not'.
Similar to 〜ならまだしも but slightly more dismissive.
j: 子供ならいざ知らず、大人がそんな失敗をするなんて。
e: If it were a child I wouldn't know, but for an adult to make such a mistake!

gloss: even if we assume / even for
pat: Plain form + としたところで
x: 〜としたところで is a hypothetical concessive — 'even if we assume X, Y'. Similar to 〜にしたところで and 〜としても, hedging a hypothetical and presenting a main-clause claim that holds regardless. Formal / literary register.
notes: Formal hypothetical concession.
Similar to 〜にしたところで and 〜としても.
j: 仮に成功したとしたところで、喜べない。
e: Even if we assume it succeeded, I can't be happy.

gloss: of such a degree / to the extent of (a)
pat: Noun / plain form + ほどの + noun
x: 〜ほどの + noun expresses that the following noun has the degree or extent of X — 'a noun of the extent / caliber of X'. Used to describe high-degree qualities or notable examples. Formal / literary register.
notes: Extent modifier — describes a noun with the degree of X.
Common: 涙が出るほどの感動 ('emotion to the extent of tears'), これほどの大事件 ('an incident of this magnitude').
j: これほどの大事件は初めてだ。
e: An incident of this magnitude is a first.

gloss: unnecessary / better left unsaid
pat: V negative stem + ずもがな
x: 〜ずもがな is a literary construction meaning 'unnecessary' or 'better left undone' — what's described is better not done. Often with verbs of speaking: 言わずもがな ('needless to say / better left unsaid'). Very literary, almost fixed-phrase register.
notes: Literary / classical — 'better left undone / unsaid'.
Almost exclusively in fixed phrases, most commonly 言わずもがな.
j: 言わずもがなのことを言ってしまった。
e: I said something that would have been better left unsaid.

gloss: will definitely do / I'll show you (determination)
x: 〜てみせる expresses the speaker's determination to accomplish something — 'I'll definitely do X (and show you I can)'. Different from 〜てみる (try doing) in that みせる literally means 'to show', expressing pride or defiance about proving capability. Used in dramatic or resolute declarations.
notes: Determined declaration — 'I'll show you / prove I can'.
Often in challenging contexts: 絶対に合格してみせる ('I'll definitely pass, you'll see').
j: 絶対に合格してみせる。
e: I'll definitely pass, you'll see.

gloss: there's a limit to / (X) goes too far
pat: Noun / V plain + にもほどがある
x: 〜にもほどがある expresses criticism that X goes beyond acceptable bounds — 'there's a limit to X (and you've exceeded it)'. Often used as a strong complaint or scolding. Can follow nouns or plain forms. Neutral / casual register with emotional emphasis.
notes: Strong complaint — X has gone too far.
Common in criticism: 冗談にもほどがある ('there's a limit to jokes'), 嘘にもほどがある.
j: 冗談にもほどがある。
e: There's a limit to joking — this has gone too far.

gloss: not worth / insufficient for / unworthy of
pat: Noun / V dict-form + に足りない
x: 〜に足りない is a negation of 〜に足る (worth), expressing that something is 'not worth X' or 'unworthy of X'. More dismissive variant of 〜に足る. Common with nouns of evaluation: 信頼に足りない ('not worthy of trust'), 恐れるに足りない ('not worth fearing'). Formal / literary register.
notes: Negation of 〜に足る — 'not worth X'.
Common fixed phrases: 信頼に足りない, 恐れるに足りない, 取るに足りない.
j: それは取るに足りないことだ。
e: That's not worth mentioning.

gloss: combining / at the same time / also as
pat: V ます-stem / noun + かたがた
x: 〜かたがた expresses that an action serves two purposes at once — 'combining X with Y' / 'taking the opportunity to do both'. Similar in function to 〜がてら but more formal. Often used in polite correspondence about visits or gifts: お礼かたがた ('serving also as thanks'). Formal / literary register.
notes: Formal / polite 'serving two purposes at once'.
More formal than 〜がてら (N1 also).
j: お礼かたがた、ご挨拶に伺います。
e: I will visit you for a greeting, which also serves as thanks.

gloss: about to / trying to / on the verge of (literary)
x: 〜んとする is a literary / archaic construction meaning 'about to X' or 'trying to X'. Uses the classical volitional form with する. Very formal / literary, rarely in casual speech. Common fixed forms: 言わんとする ('trying to say'), 飛び去らんとする ('on the verge of flying away').
notes: Literary / classical — modern equivalent is 〜ようとする.
Common fixed forms: 言わんとする, 消えんとする, 死なんとする.
j: 彼の言わんとするところを理解した。
e: I understood what he was trying to say.

gloss: no doubt / certainly / I'm sure
x: 〜に相違ない is a formal / literary equivalent of 〜に違いない ('must be'), expressing strong conviction — 'there is no doubt that X'. The noun 相違 literally means 'difference / discrepancy'. Very formal, common in written reports and formal analyses.
notes: Formal / literary equivalent of 〜に違いない.
Very common in formal writing: news, reports, essays.
j: 彼が犯人に相違ない。
e: There's no doubt he's the culprit.

gloss: if it's (a case of) / given that it is
pat: Plain form / noun + とあっては
x: 〜とあっては expresses a conditional based on a specific circumstance — 'if it's the case that X, (then Y follows)'. Often used for commitments or required responses given a special situation. Close to 〜とあれば but with a slightly stronger case-making flavor. Formal / literary register.
notes: Conditional case-making — 'if it's a case of X, then Y'.
Close to 〜とあれば (covered at N2) — とあっては is slightly more insistent.
j: 緊急事態とあっては、すぐ駆けつけなければならない。
e: If it's an emergency, I have to rush over right away.

gloss: if only / you should have (regret)
x: 〜ものを expresses the speaker's regret or frustration that someone didn't do what would have been sensible — 'if only you had X' / 'you should have X, but didn't'. Literary register, often with an emotional / scolding nuance. Common paired with 〜たら / 〜ば.
notes: Regret / frustration over someone's inaction or wrong action.
Often paired with conditional: 言ってくれたらよかったものを ('if only you had told me').
j: 早く言ってくれればよかったものを。
e: If only you had told me sooner.

gloss: regard as / consider as / deem to be
pat: Noun / plain form + とみなす
x: 〜とみなす expresses a formal judgment or designation — 'regard as X' / 'deem to be X'. Common in legal, business, and policy contexts for making categorical decisions. The verb 見なす literally means 'to regard / consider'. Formal / official register.
notes: Formal / official designation — 'for the purposes of X, consider Y to be Z'.
Common in legal and policy: 〜とみなされる ('is deemed to be').
j: 無断欠席は退学とみなされる。
e: Unexcused absence will be regarded as withdrawal.

gloss: not content with / not satisfied with (and seeking more)
pat: Noun / plain form + に飽き足らず
x: 〜に飽き足らず expresses that the subject is not content with X and seeks or does Y in addition — 'not satisfied with X, (they also pursue Y)'. Literary register, often in narratives of ambition or drive.
notes: Ambition / drive — subject wants more than X.
Common in narratives of achievement: 現状に飽き足らず, 国内に飽き足らず.
j: 彼は現状に飽き足らず、新しい挑戦を始めた。
e: Not content with the status quo, he began a new challenge.

gloss: inevitably / as one would expect / destined to
x: 〜べくして is a literary construction expressing that something happened inevitably or as fate would have it — 'destined to X'. Often with the same verb repeated: 起こるべくして起こった ('happened as it was bound to happen'). Very literary register.
notes: Literary inevitability — 'as fate would have it'.
Often with same verb repeated: 起こるべくして起こる, 勝つべくして勝つ.
j: この事件は起こるべくして起こった。
e: This incident happened as it was destined to happen.

gloss: only / just (literary)
x: 〜のみ is a literary / formal particle meaning 'only' — the formal equivalent of だけ. Very common in formal writing, legal documents, and official announcements. Can attach directly to nouns or plain-form predicates.
notes: Literary 'only' — formal equivalent of だけ.
Common in legal and official contexts.
j: 会員のみ入場できます。
e: Only members may enter.

gloss: no need to / not necessary to / not up to
pat: V dict / noun + には及ばない
x: 〜には及ばない has two senses: (1) 'no need to X' — often in polite dismissal (心配には及びません 'there's no need to worry'); (2) 'does not measure up to / cannot match' — comparing abilities or qualities. Formal / polite register.
notes: Two senses — 'no need to' (dismissive) and 'cannot match' (comparative).
Common fixed phrase: 心配には及びません ('no need to worry').
j: ご心配には及びません。
e: There's no need for concern.

gloss: there's no end to / (if you list X) it would be endless
x: 〜たらきりがない expresses that there is no end / no limit to X if one were to continue — 'there's no end to listing / doing X'. Often used when the speaker wants to stop listing or discussing because the list would be endless. Conversational register.
notes: Endless list / action — 'could go on forever'.
Common fixed phrase: 〜を挙げたらきりがない ('the list would be endless').
j: 欠点を挙げたらきりがない。
e: If you list the flaws, there's no end.

gloss: is considered / is said to be
pat: Plain form + とされる / とされている
x: 〜とされる is a formal passive expression meaning 'is considered / regarded as'. Common in academic writing, news, and official statements — it presents X as a widely-held view without specifying who holds it. The progressive とされている emphasizes ongoing / current consensus.
notes: Passive / impersonal 'is regarded as'.
Common in academic and formal writing.
j: 彼は天才とされている。
e: He is considered a genius.

gloss: seems to be / presumed to be
pat: Plain form + とおぼしい / とおぼしき
x: 〜とおぼしい is a literary / archaic evidential meaning 'seems to be' or 'presumed to be'. The attributive form とおぼしき + noun is common in narrative descriptions where the speaker is guessing identity or nature. Very literary register, rare in casual speech.
notes: Literary evidential — 'seems / presumed'.
The attributive form とおぼしき is most common.
j: 犯人とおぼしき男が現場から逃げた。
e: A man presumed to be the culprit fled the scene.

gloss: although / even while / despite
pat: V ます-stem / i-adj / noun + ながらも
x: 〜ながらも is a literary concessive meaning 'although / even while X, Y'. Similar to 〜ながら (simultaneous) but with concessive nuance — the main clause is unexpected or contrasting. Formal / literary register.
notes: Concessive — 'although X, Y'.
Distinct from 〜ながら (neutral simultaneity).
j: 小さいながらも、立派な家だ。
e: Small though it is, it's a splendid house.

gloss: if it comes to / in the event that
x: 〜となれば presents a hypothetical scenario and the consequence that would follow — 'if it comes to X, (then) Y'. More hypothetical / formal than 〜たら or 〜なら. Common in planning, discussing contingencies, or setting up a hypothetical that leads to a necessary action.
notes: Formal hypothetical — 'if the situation reaches X'.
Main clause typically describes an obligatory or natural consequence.
j: 留学するとなれば、準備が必要だ。
e: If it comes to studying abroad, preparation is necessary.

gloss: when it comes to / if it's a matter of
x: 〜となると introduces a topic or scenario and its expected consequence — 'when it comes to X, (the situation changes)'. Often used when the speaker realizes the implications of a stated scenario. Close in meaning to 〜となれば but slightly more conversational and often signals a shift in the speaker's perspective.
notes: Perspective-shifting — 'now that we're talking about X...'.
Close to 〜となれば but slightly less formal / more conversational.
j: 留学となると、お金が心配だ。
e: When it comes to studying abroad, I worry about money.

gloss: just as / like / as if (literary)
pat: Plain form / noun + の + ごとく
x: 〜ごとく is a literary / classical construction meaning 'just as' or 'like' — used for similes and comparisons in formal and literary writing. Derived from the classical adjective ごとし. Very formal, common in literature, essays, and formal speeches. Attributive form ごとき + noun is also productive.
notes: Literary / classical simile marker — 'just as'.
Very formal / written register.
j: 矢のごとく、時間が過ぎていく。
e: Time passes just like an arrow.

gloss: worth / sufficient to / deserving of
x: 〜に足る expresses that something is worth doing or merits X — 'worth / sufficient to / deserving of'. More literary than 〜に値する ('worthy of', also N2). Often used in formal evaluations: '信頼に足る' ('worthy of trust'). The attributive 〜に足る + noun is the most common usage.
notes: Formal / literary 'worthy of'.
Common fixed phrases: 信頼に足る ('worthy of trust'), 尊敬に足る ('worthy of respect').
j: 彼は信頼に足る人物だ。
e: He is a person worthy of trust.

gloss: can bear / is worth (X-ing)
pat: Verb dict / noun + に堪える
x: 〜に堪える expresses that something is tolerable or worth X — 'can bear X / is worth X'. Often used with verbs of evaluation, viewing, or listening: 見るに堪える ('worth watching / bearable to watch'). The negated form 〜に堪えない (see separate entry) is more common and means 'unbearable'.
notes: Tolerance / worth — 'is worth bearing'.
More common in negated form 〜に堪えない (see separate entry).
j: この作品は鑑賞に堪える。
e: This work is worth appreciating.

gloss: unbearable / can't bear to / not worth
pat: Verb dict / noun + に堪えない
x: 〜に堪えない is the negation of 〜に堪える — 'unbearable to X' or 'not worth X-ing'. Common with evaluation verbs: 見るに堪えない ('unbearable to watch'), 聞くに堪えない ('unbearable to listen to'). Also used for emotional states: 感慨に堪えない ('overcome with emotion').
notes: Negated form of 〜に堪える — unbearability or 'not worth'.
Common with evaluation: 見るに堪えない, 聞くに堪えない.
j: その映画はひどすぎて、見るに堪えなかった。
e: The movie was so bad it was unbearable to watch.

gloss: although / even though (literary)
x: 〜といえども is a formal / literary concessive meaning 'even though X' or 'although X'. Often used when the speaker acknowledges that X is the case but presents a contrasting main clause. More formal than 〜とはいえ. Common in speeches, essays, and literary writing.
notes: Very formal / literary concessive — rare in casual speech.
More formal than 〜とはいえ or 〜にしても.
j: 子供といえども、約束は守るべきだ。
e: Even a child should keep a promise.

gloss: but contrary to expectation / I thought but
x: 〜と思いきや expresses that the speaker's expectation was contradicted by reality — 'I thought X, but (the reality was Y)'. Literary register. Often used in narratives for surprising reversals of expectation.
notes: Surprise reversal — expectation contradicted by reality.
Literary / narrative register.
j: 簡単と思いきや、意外に難しかった。
e: I thought it would be easy, but it was surprisingly hard.

gloss: as soon as / the moment that (literary)
x: 〜が早いか is a literary construction expressing that two events happen in near-immediate succession — 'as soon as / the moment X happens, Y'. Very similar in function to 〜や否や and 〜なり (literary 'as soon as'). Formal / literary register, rare in casual speech.
notes: Literary 'as soon as' — similar to や否や, なり, か〜ないかのうちに.
Very formal / literary register — common in narratives and dramatic prose.
j: ベルが鳴るが早いか、生徒たちは走り出した。
e: The moment the bell rang, the students ran out.

gloss: should be (fittingly) / ought to be
pat: V-て form + しかるべき
x: 〜てしかるべき expresses that an action or state 'should be' or 'is fitting' — 'ought to be done' with a sense of fairness or propriety. Very formal / literary register, common in formal criticism and arguments about what should be done. The verb しかる is literary for 'to be fitting'.
notes: Formal / literary 'ought to be'.
Implies fairness or propriety — what 'ought' fittingly to happen.
j: 彼には謝罪があってしかるべきだ。
e: There ought to be an apology from him.

gloss: prior to / in advance of
pat: V plain / noun + に先立って / に先立ち
x: 〜に先立って marks an action taken BEFORE an important upcoming event — 'prior to X, Y'. It is formal and usually appears in business and official contexts where preparation is explicit. The Y clause is the preparatory action; the X clause is the anticipated main event.
notes: Formal / business register — for preparatory actions before an important event.
にさきだち is a slightly more literary variant.
j: 会議に先立って、資料を配布した。
e: Prior to the meeting, I distributed the materials.

gloss: triggered by / with X as the impetus
pat: Noun / V plain + をきっかけに(して)
x: 〜をきっかけに introduces a triggering event that led to a significant change or new action — 'triggered by X, Y began / happened'. Often used for life-changing moments: a trip, a book, a meeting that sparked a new direction. Less formal than 〜を契機に.
notes: Emphasizes the triggering moment — often something small or incidental that led to something big.
Less formal than 〜を契機に (which is more literary).
j: 日本旅行をきっかけに、日本語を勉強し始めた。
e: A trip to Japan triggered my starting to study Japanese.
_k: 書くをきっかけに(して)

gloss: because / therefore (literary)
pat: Plain form + (が)ゆえに / 故に
x: 〜ゆえに is a literary / archaic causal marker meaning 'because X, therefore Y'. It is used in essays, formal writing, legal / philosophical texts, and classical styles. Modern speech rarely uses it, preferring から or ので. The standalone sentence-initial ゆえに can mean 'therefore'.
notes: Literary / archaic register — rarely used in modern speech.
Common in legal, philosophical, and academic writing.
j: 我思う、ゆえに我あり。
e: I think, therefore I am.

gloss: from the fact that / based on the fact
x: 〜ことから presents a fact or evidence as the basis for a conclusion, explanation, or designation — 'from the fact that X, (Y follows)'. Often used to explain the origin of a name, reputation, or conclusion drawn from observed evidence. Formal / written register.
notes: Evidence-based conclusion — X is the factual basis for Y.
Common in etymological / naming explanations: 桜の木が多いことから、この場所は'桜町'と呼ばれている.
j: 桜の木が多いことから、この町は'桜町'と呼ばれている。
e: From the fact that it has many cherry trees, this town is called 'Sakura Town'.

gloss: out of excess / from too much
pat: V plain / i-adj / na-adj な / noun の + あまり
x: 〜あまり expresses an excessive degree of emotion, sensation, or state that led to the main-clause consequence — 'out of too much X, Y happened'. Often with emotional nouns (驚き, 嬉しさ, 悲しみ) or strong verbs. Formal / written register. The main clause is typically an intense or unusual reaction.
notes: Expresses an excess of emotion / sensation leading to an unusual result.
Common with nominalized emotions: 驚きのあまり, 嬉しさのあまり, 悲しみのあまり.
j: 驚きのあまり、言葉を失った。
e: Out of sheer surprise, I was lost for words.

gloss: precisely because / it is exactly because
x: 〜からこそ emphasizes that the X clause is the essential and exclusive reason for Y — 'precisely because X, Y (and no other reason)'. More common than 〜ばこそ in modern speech, and slightly less literary. Often used in heartfelt reasoning, explanations, and endorsements.
notes: Common variant of 〜ばこそ — より neutral register.
Emphasizes that X is the essential reason, ruling out other potential causes.
j: 大切な友達だからこそ、厳しいことも言う。
e: It's precisely because you're a dear friend that I say harsh things too.

gloss: accompanying / along with / as X progresses
pat: Noun / V plain + に伴って / に伴い
x: 〜に伴って expresses that one change or event accompanies another — 'along with X, Y also (happens / changes)'. Similar to 〜につれて and 〜にしたがって, but slightly more formal and with a stronger 'accompaniment' feel. Common in descriptions of social, economic, and environmental changes.
notes: Formal register — common in news, reports, and academic writing.
に伴い is the slightly more literary variant.
j: 少子化に伴って、学校が減っている。
e: Along with the declining birthrate, the number of schools is decreasing.

gloss: despite / in spite of / even though
pat: Plain form + にもかかわらず
x: 〜にもかかわらず is a formal concessive marker meaning 'despite X, Y'. More formal than のに or が, with no emotional connotation — purely contrastive. Common in written Japanese, news, and formal speech. The main clause presents an unexpected or counter-intuitive continuation.
notes: Formal concessive — neutral tone, no emotional weight.
More formal than のに (which can carry frustration) and が (neutral but less emphatic).
j: 悪天候にもかかわらず、試合は行われた。
e: Despite the bad weather, the match was held.

gloss: can't afford to be (doing X) / can't stay (in state X)
x: 〜てはいられない expresses that the speaker cannot afford to remain in a state or continue doing an action due to urgency or pressing concerns — 'I can't afford to be sitting around'. Often used when the speaker feels compelled to act because of an unfolding situation.
notes: Urgency / pressing concern — the speaker can't stay inactive.
Casual contraction: 〜ちゃいられない (食べてはいられない → 食べちゃいられない).
j: こうしてはいられない。早く行こう。
e: I can't just stay like this. Let's hurry.

gloss: even if / whether or not (formal)
pat: Plain form + にしろ / にせよ
x: 〜にしろ / 〜にせよ are formal literary variants of 〜にしても ('even if'). They can appear singly as a concessive, or in paired form (X にしろ Y にしろ — 'whether X or Y, either way'). More formal than 〜にしても and 〜ても. Common in formal / written Japanese.
notes: Formal / literary variants of にしても.
Paired use (X にしろ Y にしろ) expresses 'whether X or Y, the point is...'.
j: 行くにしろ行かないにしろ、早く決めてください。
e: Whether you go or not, please decide quickly.

gloss: even if / even assuming / even as
x: 〜としても is a concessive marker meaning 'even if X', 'even assuming X'. It hypothetically accepts X and then states something that would hold regardless. More formal than 〜ても, with a slightly more analytical / considered feel. Can also mean 'even as (in the capacity of X)' when the preceding is a noun.
notes: Hypothetical concession — 'even if we accept that X, Y'.
Noun sense: 教師としても、親としても ('even as a teacher / even as a parent').
j: 失敗したとしても、経験にはなる。
e: Even if I fail, it will become experience.

gloss: regardless of / no matter (what / who / how)
pat: Verb volitional + と / ようと
x: Verb volitional + と / ようと is a concessive construction — 'no matter what X', 'regardless of X'. Often paired with interrogatives (誰, 何, どこ) to express 'no matter who / what / where'. Formal / literary register. The paired form 〜うと〜まいと (see separate entry) covers 'whether or not'.
notes: Formal / literary concessive.
Common with interrogatives: 誰が何と言おうと ('no matter what anyone says').
j: 誰が何と言おうと、私は諦めない。
e: No matter what anyone says, I won't give up.

gloss: do X to the very end / thoroughly
x: 〜抜く is an auxiliary meaning 'do X through to completion / to the very end'. Implies determination and often hardship — the action is completed despite difficulty. Common with endurance verbs: 走り抜く ('run through to the end'), 考え抜く ('think through thoroughly'), 生き抜く ('live through / survive').
notes: Emphasizes completion despite difficulty or hardship.
Common with endurance / effort verbs: 走り抜く, 考え抜く, 生き抜く, 守り抜く.
j: 最後まで走り抜いた。
e: I ran through to the very end.

gloss: hard to do (emotionally / uncomfortably)
x: 〜づらい is a suffix meaning 'hard / uncomfortable to do X', with a focus on emotional or psychological difficulty rather than physical difficulty. Distinct from 〜にくい (physical difficulty) and 〜がたい (formal, often moral difficulty). Common for actions that cause discomfort, awkwardness, or emotional resistance.
notes: Emotional / psychological difficulty — 'awkward to do'.
Contrast with 〜にくい (physical difficulty) and 〜がたい (formal / moral).
j: それは少し言いづらい話だ。
e: That's a bit of an awkward topic to bring up.

gloss: hard / difficult to (formal)
x: 〜がたい is a formal / literary suffix meaning 'hard to X' or 'difficult to X', often with a moral or intellectual nuance — things that are hard to accept, believe, or forgive. Distinct from 〜にくい (physical / practical difficulty) and 〜づらい (emotional discomfort). Functions as an i-adjective.
notes: Formal / literary — moral or intellectual difficulty.
Common fixed forms: 信じがたい ('hard to believe'), 想像しがたい ('hard to imagine'), 許しがたい ('hard to forgive').
j: それは信じがたい話だ。
e: That's a hard-to-believe story.

gloss: (it's) as expected from / lives up to
pat: Plain form + だけのことはある
x: 〜だけのことはある expresses that the main-clause praise or quality is fitting given a stated premise — 'being X, it's no surprise that Y' / 'Y lives up to the expectations of X'. Positive evaluative, very similar to 〜だけあって (N3) but in a slightly more emphatic, reflective tone.
notes: Positive evaluative — praise that 'fits' the premise.
Very close in meaning to 〜だけあって (N3); this form is more reflective / conclusive.
j: 長年練習しただけのことはある。演奏が素晴らしい。
e: The years of practice have paid off. The performance is wonderful.
_k: 書くだけのことはある

gloss: that's what X is / that's (the nature of) X
pat: Plain form + というものだ
x: 〜というものだ expresses a speaker's evaluative conclusion or universal statement about what something is or should be — 'that's what X is' / 'that's the way of things'. Often carries a moralizing or reflective tone, stating a general truth or principle. Distinct from 〜ものだ (general tendency / nostalgic 'used to') — というものだ is more evaluative.
notes: Evaluative / normative — 'that's the nature of it'.
Often preceded by a definition or statement the speaker is reframing.
j: 困っている人を助けるのが友情というものだ。
e: Helping a friend in need — that's what friendship is.

gloss: it's not simply (a matter of) / it's not that
pat: Plain form + というものではない
x: 〜というものではない negates a simplistic claim, arguing that the situation is more nuanced than the stated X — 'it's not simply that X' / 'it doesn't just come down to X'. Common in discussions where the speaker is correcting an oversimplification.
notes: Corrects an oversimplification — insists on nuance.
Common in arguments and essays that resist easy conclusions.
j: お金があれば幸せになれるというものではない。
e: It's not simply that having money makes you happy.
_k: 書くというものではない

gloss: because / it's because (excusing / justifying)
pat: Plain form + ものだから / もので
x: 〜ものだから gives a reason with an excuse-making or justifying flavor — 'it's because X (so please understand)'. Often used when the speaker is explaining why they did something unexpected or failed to meet an expectation. The shorter form 〜もので is slightly softer. Distinct from 〜んだから (more emphatic) and 〜から (neutral).
notes: Excuse-making — often used to explain tardiness or failures.
The short form 〜もので is softer / more polite.
j: 急いでいたものだから、挨拶もせずに帰ってしまった。
e: Because I was in a hurry, I left without even saying goodbye.

gloss: things like X and Y (disordered / overwhelming)
pat: Noun + やら + noun + やら
x: 〜やら〜やら is a non-exhaustive list construction similar to 〜とか〜とか, but with a flavor of disarray, overwhelm, or mess. Often used when describing a situation as chaotic or a mix of unpleasant items — 'what with X and Y'. Can also combine adjectives or verb plain forms. Formal / literary register compared to とか.
notes: Disordered / overwhelmed list — often describing a messy situation.
More formal / literary than とか.
j: 宿題やら掃除やらで忙しい。
e: I'm busy with homework and cleaning and whatnot.

gloss: now that / since (with strong obligation)
x: 〜からには expresses a strong commitment based on a premise — 'now that X, one must Y'. The main clause typically expresses obligation, determination, or strong consequence arising from the X premise. Similar in function to 〜以上は but with slightly more emotional weight. Formal register.
notes: Strong obligation from a premise — 'since this is the case, you must'.
Similar to 〜以上(は) but emotionally stronger.
j: 約束したからには、必ず守ります。
e: Now that I've promised, I will definitely keep it.

gloss: not only X but also Y (literary)
x: 〜のみならず is a literary 'not only' construction — the most formal variant of the 'not only' family (〜だけでなく, 〜ばかりでなく, 〜のみならず). Common in essays, formal speeches, and written Japanese. Often paired with も in the main clause.
notes: Most formal / literary of the 'not only' family.
Rare in casual speech — common in essays, news, and formal writing.
j: 彼は頭がいいのみならず、性格もいい。
e: Not only is he smart, but he also has a good personality.

gloss: although / that said / even so
x: 〜とはいえ is a formal concessive meaning 'although X' or 'that said, X'. It hedges a statement by noting that while X is true, the main clause presents a contrasting or tempering observation. Literary / formal register, common in essays and written Japanese.
notes: Literary / formal concessive — 'that said'.
Common in essays, news, and balanced discussions.
j: もう春とはいえ、まだ寒い。
e: Although it's already spring, it's still cold.

gloss: that said / although one says
pat: Plain form + とはいうものの
x: 〜とはいうものの is a literary concessive similar to 〜とはいえ — 'although one says X, (the reality is Y)'. Often used to qualify a general statement by pointing out exceptions or nuances. More drawn-out and reflective than 〜とはいえ. Common in written Japanese.
notes: Reflective / nuance-adding concessive.
More drawn-out than とはいえ — emphasizes the speaker's consideration.
j: 春だとはいうものの、今朝は雪が降った。
e: Although we say it's spring, snow fell this morning.

gloss: just because / even though (one says)
pat: Plain form + からといって
x: 〜からといって rejects a simplistic causal inference — 'just because X (doesn't mean Y)'. The main clause often uses a negative or 'not necessarily' predicate to refute the naive inference. Very common in careful reasoning and avoiding overgeneralization.
notes: Rejects a simple 'X therefore Y' inference — 'just because X, doesn't mean Y'.
Main clause usually hedged: とは限らない, わけではない.
j: お金があるからといって、幸せとは限らない。
e: Just because you have money doesn't necessarily mean you're happy.

gloss: in the process of / gradually becoming
pat: Verb ます-stem + つつある
x: 〜つつある expresses that an action or change is currently in progress or gradually happening — 'is in the process of X'. Often used for large-scale, long-term, or gradual changes (social, environmental, personal). More formal than 〜ている (which is the everyday progressive). Common in reports and formal descriptions of trends.
notes: Formal progressive — for gradual or ongoing change.
Common with change verbs: 変わる, 増える, 減る, 発展する, 進む.
j: 地球温暖化が進みつつある。
e: Global warming is progressing.

gloss: at least X (is better than nothing) / could be worse
x: 〜だけましだ expresses a minor consolation — 'at least X is the case, and that's better than worse alternatives'. Used when finding a silver lining in a negative situation: it's not great, but at least it's not as bad as it could be. The main clause often implicitly or explicitly compares to a worse hypothetical.
notes: Minor consolation — silver lining in a negative situation.
Often with implicit comparison to something worse.
j: 雨だけど、雪じゃないだけましだ。
e: It's raining, but at least it's not snowing.

gloss: as soon as / immediately after (with repeated undoing)
pat: Verb plain / V-た form + そばから
x: 〜そばから expresses 'no sooner had X happened than Y undid it' — a repetitive cycle where an action is immediately negated or reversed by another. Common for frustrating situations of never-ending effort: 'as soon as I clean it, it gets dirty again'. Often carries a tone of exasperation.
notes: Repetitive / futile effort — the main clause undoes the X action.
Common in frustration / exasperation: 教えたそばから忘れる ('as soon as I teach him, he forgets').
j: 教えたそばから忘れてしまう。
e: He forgets as soon as I teach him.

gloss: it's not as if / since it's not like
pat: Noun / plain form + じゃあるまいし
x: 〜じゃあるまいし expresses 'it's not as if X, so (you should act accordingly)' — a construction that rejects a childish or unreasonable premise. Often used to correct or scold: 'you're not a child, so...' The more formal written form is 〜ではあるまいし.
notes: Rejects an unreasonable premise — often used to correct or scold.
Common fixed type: 子供じゃあるまいし ('you're not a child, are you?').
j: 子供じゃあるまいし、そんなことで泣かないで。
e: You're not a child — don't cry over that.

gloss: as if to say / seemingly saying
pat: Plain form / phrase + とばかりに
x: 〜とばかりに expresses that someone's action or behavior seems to convey a specific message, without them actually saying it — 'as if to say X'. Common in describing body language, facial expressions, or strong non-verbal signals. Formal / literary register.
notes: Describes non-verbal communication — actions that convey a message.
Often with strong gestures or looks: 怒ったとばかりに, 嬉しいとばかりに.
j: 彼は「もう限界だ」とばかりに、ため息をついた。
e: He sighed as if to say 'I've had enough'.

gloss: if it's (a case of) / if it's for
pat: Noun / plain form + とあれば
x: 〜とあれば expresses a hypothetical or conditional framing — 'if it is the case of X' / 'if it's for X'. Often carries a sense of willingness to act for a specific cause: 'if it's for my family, I'd do anything'. Formal / literary register, common in formal declarations of commitment.
notes: Formal / literary hypothetical.
Often paired with a willing commitment: あなたのためとあれば、何でもする ('if it's for you, I'd do anything').
j: あなたのためとあれば、何でもする。
e: If it's for you, I'll do anything.

gloss: doesn't look like / there's no sign of
pat: Verb ます-stem + そうにない / そうもない
x: 〜そうにない / 〜そうもない is the negative of the appearance-based そうだ — 'doesn't look like X will happen'. Common with future predictions: the speaker sees no evidence that X will occur. More emphatic than ないだろう. Distinct from the hearsay negative construction.
notes: Appearance-based negation — no sign of X happening.
そうもない is slightly more emphatic than そうにない.
j: 雨が降りそうにない。
e: It doesn't look like it's going to rain.

gloss: ended up not (doing) / didn't manage to
pat: V negative stem + ずじまい
x: 〜ずじまい expresses regret that an intended action was not carried out — 'ended up not X-ing'. Common in retrospectives: 'I meant to do X, but in the end didn't'. Carries a note of disappointment or missed opportunity. Literary / formal register.
notes: Retrospective regret — 'didn't end up X-ing, though I meant to'.
Irregular: する → せずじまい (not しずじまい).
j: 忙しくて、彼に会えずじまいだった。
e: I was so busy I didn't manage to see him.

gloss: on the other hand / while (one side)
x: 〜反面 presents two contrasting aspects of the same subject — 'on the one hand X, on the other Y'. Functionally similar to 〜一方で (N3) but with a stronger 'two sides of a coin' feel. Formal / neutral register, common in balanced descriptions of pros and cons.
notes: 'Two sides of the same thing' — often used for pros/cons or complementary aspects.
Similar to 〜一方で — choice is stylistic.
j: この仕事は給料がいい反面、責任が重い。
e: This job has good pay, but on the other hand, heavy responsibility.

gloss: I hear that / it means that
pat: Plain form + ということだ
x: 〜ということだ has two related senses: (1) hearsay / report — 'I hear that X' / 'they say X'; (2) meaning / conclusion — 'it means X'. Context disambiguates. Common in news reports and in drawing conclusions from preceding statements. Formal register.
notes: Hearsay sense: 'I hear / it is said that'. Common in news.
Meaning sense: 'in other words' — summarizing a preceding explanation.
j: ニュースによると、明日は雨が降るということだ。
e: According to the news, it's going to rain tomorrow.

gloss: as a result of / after
pat: V-た form / noun + の + 結果
x: 〜結果 (けっか) introduces the result or outcome of a process — 'as a result of X, Y'. Formal / written register, common in reports, essays, and formal narratives. The attributive form 結果の + noun is also productive.
notes: Formal / written — typical of reports, news, and academic writing.
Common with process verbs: 調査した結果, 議論の結果, 話し合いの結果.
j: 調査した結果、新しい事実が分かった。
e: As a result of our investigation, new facts came to light.

gloss: on the occasion of / at the time of (formal)
pat: V plain / noun + の + 際(に)
x: 〜際(に) marks a significant occasion or moment when something is done — 'on the occasion of X, Y'. More formal than 〜とき and less ceremonial than 〜にあたって. Common in formal announcements, instructions, and business communications: 'in case of emergency, call this number'.
notes: Formal temporal marker — for significant moments or occasions.
More formal than 〜とき; less ceremonial than 〜にあたって.
j: 非常の際は、このボタンを押してください。
e: In case of emergency, press this button.

gloss: just as / according to / exactly like
x: 〜通り / 〜どおり expresses that an action or outcome is exactly as X was described, predicted, or specified — 'just as X', 'according to X'. The reading shifts between とおり and どおり depending on the preceding word: どおり after nouns (予定どおり), とおり after verb plain forms (言ったとおり).
notes: Reading depends on the base: noun + どおり (voiced), verb + とおり (unvoiced).
Common: 予定どおり, 指示どおり, 思ったとおり, 言ったとおり.
j: 予定どおりに出発した。
e: We departed just as planned.

gloss: because it's / given that it's (special situation)
x: 〜とあって expresses that the main-clause phenomenon is occurring because of a special circumstance X — 'because it's X (a notable situation), the result is Y'. The X clause is typically a notable or unusual situation, and the main clause describes a resulting atmosphere or behavior. Formal / written register.
notes: Causal — the X situation is unusual / notable and explains the main clause.
Main clause often describes crowds, atmosphere, or unusual behavior.
j: 休日とあって、公園は大勢の人で賑わった。
e: Being a holiday, the park was crowded with many people.

gloss: it seems that / appears to
x: 〜とみえる expresses that something appears to be the case based on observable evidence — 'it seems that X'. Similar to 〜ようだ but with a more observational / neutral feel. Formal / literary register. The と is the quotation/thought particle.
notes: Observational inference — based on evidence the speaker can see.
Close in meaning to 〜ようだ, 〜らしい, 〜みたい — as another evidential.
j: 彼は忙しいとみえる。
e: It seems he is busy.

gloss: supposing / assuming / if it's the case that
pat: Plain form + とすれば / とすると / としたら
x: 〜とすれば (with variants 〜とすると, 〜としたら) expresses a hypothetical assumption — 'supposing that X, then Y'. The speaker accepts X as a premise for the sake of argument and draws a consequence. Formal / neutral register, common in analytical discussions and planning.
notes: Hypothetical assumption — 'assuming X, then Y'.
Three variants: とすれば (slightly more formal), とすると (neutral), としたら (slightly more conversational).
j: もし雨が降るとすれば、どうしますか。
e: Supposing it rains, what will you do?

gloss: is nothing more than / merely
pat: Noun / plain form + にすぎない
x: 〜にすぎない expresses that something is 'nothing more than X' — a dismissive or minimizing description. Common for downplaying the significance of something: 'it's just an excuse', 'it's merely a rumor'. The verb すぎる means 'exceed / go beyond'; the negative form 'not exceed' means 'is no more than'.
notes: Dismissive / minimizing — 'nothing more than X'.
Common with 言い訳 ('excuse'), 噂 ('rumor'), 推測 ('guess'), 一例 ('one example').
j: それは単なる言い訳にすぎない。
e: That's nothing more than a mere excuse.

gloss: since / because (formal, explanatory)
pat: Plain form / noun + の + こととて
x: 〜こととて is a formal / literary reason marker — 'since X is the case, Y (please excuse)'. Often used in apologies or explanations to acknowledge that circumstances caused an imperfection: 'since I'm new, please forgive any mistakes'. Very formal, rarely used in casual speech.
notes: Formal / literary causal — apologetic register.
Very common in polite apologies: 初めてのこととて, 急なこととて.
j: 初めてのこととて、不手際をお許しください。
e: Since it's my first time, please forgive any mishandling.

gloss: not worth that much / not such a big deal
pat: Plain form + ほどのことではない / ほどのものではない
x: 〜ほどのことではない dismisses a situation or action as not deserving a strong reaction — 'it's not that big a deal', 'not worth getting upset about'. Often used to calm down someone who is overreacting, or to express humility about one's own achievements. Neutral / formal register.
notes: Dismissive / minimizing — downplays significance.
Often used in reassurance: 心配するほどのことではない ('nothing to worry about').
j: 心配するほどのことではないよ。
e: It's not worth worrying about.
_k: 書くほどのことではない

gloss: even without / even if not
x: 〜ずとも is a formal / literary concessive meaning 'even without doing X' or 'even if not X'. Combines the formal negative ず with the concessive とも. Less common than the equivalent 〜なくても but appears in literature, formal speeches, and fixed expressions. Irregular: する → せずとも.
notes: Formal / literary equivalent of 〜なくても.
Irregular: する → せずとも.
j: 言わずとも分かるだろう。
e: You should understand without me saying it.

gloss: things like X and Y (complaining / disparaging listing)
pat: X だの Y だの
x: 〜だの〜だの is a non-exhaustive listing construction with a complaining or disparaging nuance — 'what with X and Y (and all that nonsense)'. Often used when the speaker is frustrated or dismissive about the listed items. Conversational register.
notes: Complaining / dismissive listing — the speaker is frustrated or exasperated.
Can list nouns, verbs, or adjectives.
j: 忙しいだの疲れただの、言い訳ばかりだ。
e: 'Busy' this, 'tired' that — nothing but excuses.

gloss: see as / regard as / judge to be
x: 〜とみる expresses that the speaker considers or judges X to be the case — 'I see it as X' / 'I regard it as X'. Formal / analytical register, common in news reports, police statements, and analytical commentary. The verb is 見る used metaphorically as 'judge / consider'.
notes: Analytical judgment — 'I regard / consider X to be the case'.
Common in news: 警察は犯人は2人組とみている ('police believe the criminals are a pair').
j: 警察は事故の原因を不注意とみている。
e: The police see the cause of the accident as negligence.

gloss: seemingly X, but actually / looks X but
pat: Plain form + ようで / ようでいて
x: 〜ようで expresses apparent contradiction — 'seemingly X, but actually Y'. The surface appearance X contrasts with the deeper reality Y. Often used for surprising insights or revelations: 'he seems quiet, but he's actually funny'. Formal / literary register.
notes: Apparent contradiction — surface vs. reality.
Common in character descriptions and surprising revelations.
j: 彼は強いようでいて、実は優しい。
e: He seems strong, but is actually gentle.

gloss: nothing in particular / nothing notable
pat: Plain form + といって / これといって
x: 〜といって (especially in the fixed form これといって) expresses that there is 'nothing in particular' worth noting — 'no specific X' / 'nothing notable'. Very commonly used to downplay or deny significance, often with negative main clauses. Neutral register, very common in everyday speech.
notes: Most commonly in the fixed phrase これといって + negative ('nothing in particular').
Downplays significance — 'nothing notable / worth mentioning'.
j: これといって問題はありません。
e: There's nothing in particular that's a problem.

gloss: if it looks like / if it appears
x: 〜ようなら is a conditional variant that attaches to hypothetical situations the speaker infers from appearance — 'if it looks like X, (then do Y)'. Often used when making contingency plans based on how things are going. Distinct from 〜なら (neutral 'if it's X').
notes: Appearance-based conditional — 'if it looks like X'.
Distinct from 〜なら (topic conditional) and 〜たら / ば (general conditional).
j: 雨が降るようなら、中止しましょう。
e: If it looks like it'll rain, let's cancel.

gloss: if it's like that / at this rate
x: 〜ようでは expresses a hypothetical condition with a negative, critical, or warning tone — 'if X is like that, (then something bad will follow)'. The main clause often presents an unfavorable prediction or judgment. Distinct from 〜ようなら (more neutral).
notes: Critical / warning conditional — implies an unfavorable outcome.
Main clause often: だめだ, 合格できない, 成功しない.
j: そんなに怠けるようでは、合格できないよ。
e: If you're lazy like that, you won't pass.

gloss: there is something (about it) / is impressively
x: 〜ものがある expresses that there is a certain quality or feature worth noting about something — 'there's something X about it'. Often used evaluatively with impressive, moving, or remarkable qualities. Formal / literary register. Different from 〜ものだ (general truth) and 〜ものの (although).
notes: Evaluative — 'there's something X about it'.
Common with impressive / emotional qualities: 感動的なものがある, 素晴らしいものがある.
j: 彼の演奏には感動的なものがある。
e: There's something moving about his performance.

gloss: what is called / the fact is / the reason is
pat: Noun / plain form + というのは
x: 〜というのは has several related senses: (1) 'what is called X / the thing called X' — introducing a definition or concept; (2) 'the fact is / the reason is' — explaining a reason or clarifying a concept. Very common as a topic marker or explanation starter. Neutral register.
notes: Definition / explanation marker — 'what X is' or 'the reason is'.
Very common in introductions and explanations.
j: 友情というのは、お金で買えないものだ。
e: Friendship is something you can't buy with money.

gloss: at the very end of / after (extensive process)
pat: V-た form / noun + の + 果てに
x: 〜果てに expresses that the main-clause outcome came at the end of a long, often harsh, process — 'after extensive X, finally Y'. Typically carries a sense of hardship or dramatic finality. Similar to 〜末に and 〜あげく but with a stronger 'far end' feel. Literary / formal register.
notes: Dramatic / final outcome after extensive effort or struggle.
Often negative or weighty — the end of a hard road.
j: 長年の努力の果てに、夢を実現した。
e: After years of effort, he finally realized his dream.

gloss: miss the chance to / fail to
pat: Verb ます-stem + そびれる
x: 〜そびれる expresses that someone missed the opportunity to do something or failed to do it despite intending to — 'miss the chance to X'. Common with things the speaker meant to do but didn't: 言いそびれる ('fail to say'), 聞きそびれる ('fail to ask'), 行きそびれる ('miss the chance to go').
notes: Missed opportunity — implies the speaker meant to but didn't.
Common with communication and travel verbs: 言う, 聞く, 行く, 会う, 帰る.
j: 言いそびれたことがある。
e: There's something I missed the chance to say.

gloss: (emphatic) not at all / definitely not (casual)
pat: V ます-stem + やしない
x: 〜やしない is a casual emphatic negative — 'definitely won't / absolutely not'. Attached to the verb ます-stem to strengthen the negation. Common in frustrated or emphatic denials. Strictly casual register.
notes: Casual emphatic negation — 'definitely won't'.
Often in frustrated complaints: 分かりやしない, 聞きやしない.
j: そんなこと、分かりやしない。
e: There's no way I'd understand that.

gloss: what it means is / so (it follows that)
pat: Plain form + ということは
x: 〜ということは is a discourse marker that introduces a logical conclusion from a preceding statement — 'what this means is', 'in other words', 'so it follows that'. Very common in spoken Japanese for drawing inferences. Distinct from 〜ということだ (hearsay / 'it means').
notes: Draws a conclusion / inference from a preceding statement.
Very common in conversation when summarizing or clarifying.
j: 彼が来ないということは、忙しいのだろう。
e: His not coming means he's probably busy.

gloss: as for whether / if you ask whether
pat: Plain form + かというと / かといえば
x: 〜かというと embeds a question for discussion — 'as for whether X, (the answer is Y)'. Often used when the speaker raises a question and then answers it themselves. Common in explanatory contexts and hedged assertions. Variants: どちらかというと ('if anything / rather').
notes: Discourse-level 'as for whether' — raising and answering a question.
Common fixed form: どちらかというと ('if anything / rather'), どちらかといえば.
j: 好きかというと、そうでもない。
e: As for whether I like it — not really.

gloss: as / regarded as / assuming that
x: 〜ものとして is used to frame something as being treated or considered as X — 'as X' or 'regarded as X'. Often in hypothetical or categorical framings: 'treat this as accepted', 'consider it settled'. Formal / written register, common in business and formal statements.
notes: Categorical framing — 'considered as X' for practical purposes.
Common in business and formal contexts.
j: 本件は合意したものとして扱います。
e: We will treat this matter as agreed upon.

gloss: enough to / to the extent that (you could)
pat: V-て form + もいいくらい
x: 〜てもいいくらい expresses that the intensity or extent of something is so high that it justifies an extreme action — 'it's so X that you might as well Y'. Often used hyperbolically. Close to 〜ほど with extreme degree meaning. Neutral / casual register.
notes: Hyperbolic degree — 'enough to do X / to the extent that'.
Often used emphatically: 感謝してもしきれないくらい ('so grateful I can't thank you enough').
j: 泣いてもいいくらい感動した。
e: I was moved enough that I could have cried.

gloss: the rest is / all that's left is
x: 〜あとは expresses that after a main action is complete, only X remains to be done — 'the rest is X' / 'all that's left is X'. Common in task-oriented contexts for summarizing what's still to be finished after the main work is done.
notes: 'Remaining to be done' — describes what's left after the main effort.
Common for project wrap-up or recipe contexts.
j: 準備はできた。あとは出発するだけだ。
e: Preparations are done. All that's left is to depart.

gloss: if only / if it's just X
pat: Noun / V plain + だけなら
x: 〜だけなら expresses 'if it's only X (then Y is OK)' — a conditional statement that limits the scope to a minimal case. Often used when the speaker is willing to accept or permit something up to a specific boundary. Neutral register.
notes: Minimal-scope conditional — 'if just X, it's fine'.
Common in permission or hedged acceptance.
j: 見るだけなら、いいですよ。
e: If it's just looking, it's fine.

gloss: not only does not / not just failing to
pat: V ない + のみならず
x: 〜ないのみならず is a literary concessive-additive combining the negative ない with the 'not only' のみならず — 'not only does X not happen, (but Y also)'. The Y clause extends the negation or adds a worse case. Formal / literary register, rare in casual speech.
notes: Literary / formal extended negation.
Common in essays and formal criticism.
j: 彼は謝らないのみならず、逆に怒り出した。
e: Not only did he not apologize, but he even got angry.

gloss: in accordance with / as (X progresses)
pat: Noun + にしたがって / V plain + にしたがって
x: 〜にしたがって has two related senses: (1) 'in accordance with' — following rules, orders, or guidelines (noun + にしたがって); (2) 'as (X progresses/increases)' — expressing a parallel change, similar to 〜につれて (V plain + にしたがって). Formal / written register, common in explanations of rules or describing progressive changes.
notes: Two senses — 'in accordance' (following rules) and 'as (X progresses)' (parallel change).
Parallel to 〜につれて — both express correlated change, but にしたがって has a slightly more formal / rule-following nuance.
j: ルールにしたがって、行動してください。
e: Please act in accordance with the rules.

gloss: although / even though (formal)
x: 〜ものの is a formal concessive marker meaning 'although X, Y', where the main clause often expresses a limitation, unexpected outcome, or reversal relative to what the ものの clause suggests. More formal and literary than けれど / が. Typical in written Japanese, reports, and formal speech. Distinct from 〜ものだ (general truth) and ものなら (if it were possible).
notes: Formal / literary register — alternatives in casual speech are けど / が.
Main clause typically expresses an unexpected continuation or limitation.
j: 宿題を始めたものの、なかなか進まない。
e: Although I started my homework, it's not progressing much.

gloss: if (it were) possible / if I could
pat: V potential form + ものなら
x: 〜ものなら combined with a potential form expresses a hypothetical wish that the speaker considers difficult or impossible — 'if I could only X'. Often accompanied by a main clause describing the desired action. Formal / literary register, with a slightly wistful tone. Distinct from 〜たら / 〜ば (general conditionals).
notes: Typically with potential forms: 会えるものなら ('if I could meet'), 戻れるものなら ('if I could go back').
Hypothetical and often wistful — implies the action is hard / impossible.
j: 昔に戻れるものなら、戻りたい。
e: If I could go back to the past, I would.

gloss: in addition to / on top of (that)
x: 〜上に is an additive connector meaning 'in addition to X, (also) Y'. The Y clause builds on or extends the X clause in the same direction — usually both positive or both negative. More formal than 〜し. Distinct from the locative 上 (above). Common in lists of reasons or attributes.
notes: Additive — Y clause extends X in the same direction (both positive or both negative).
Formal variant of 〜し (listing reasons/facts).
j: この部屋は広い上に、明るい。
e: This room is spacious and also bright.

gloss: now that / since (formal, implies commitment)
x: 〜上は (うえは) is a formal concessive / justificatory marker — 'now that X, Y must follow'. The main clause typically expresses an obligation, commitment, or necessary consequence following from the 上は premise. More formal and literary than 〜以上 (though their meanings overlap considerably). Common in business, formal writing, and speeches.
notes: Formal / literary — alternative: 〜以上(は) (slightly more common).
Main clause often expresses a required obligation or determination: 約束した上は、必ず守る.
j: 約束した上は、必ず守る。
e: Now that I've promised, I'll definitely keep my word.

gloss: since / now that / as long as
x: 〜以上(は) expresses that given the premise of the 以上 clause, a certain conclusion or obligation follows — 'since X is the case, Y'. Often used for commitments, obligations, or expectations that arise because of a stated fact. The optional は adds topic emphasis. Formal / neutral register.
notes: The premise justifies an obligation or expectation in the main clause.
Common in commitment contexts: 約束した以上、守らなければならない ('since I promised, I must keep it').
j: 約束した以上、守らなければならない。
e: Since I promised, I have to keep it.

gloss: risk of / fear that (may happen)
pat: V plain / noun + の + 恐れがある
x: 〜恐れがある expresses that there is a risk or possibility of something (usually negative) happening — 'there's a risk of X'. Common in news reports, weather forecasts, and cautionary statements. 恐れ literally means 'fear / apprehension'. Formal register.
notes: Negative risk — 'there's a risk / fear that X'.
Common in weather forecasts: 大雨の恐れがある.
j: 明日は大雨の恐れがあります。
e: There's a risk of heavy rain tomorrow.

gloss: no sooner had / just when (unexpected change)
pat: V-た form + かと思うと / かと思ったら
x: 〜かと思うと expresses that two events happen in quick succession, often with an unexpected change — 'no sooner had X than Y' / 'just when I thought X, Y happened'. Similar in function to 〜や否や and 〜たとたん, but with a stronger sense of narrative surprise. Literary register.
notes: Unexpected follow-up — two events in quick succession.
Often narrative / dramatic: 泣いたかと思うと、笑い出した ('no sooner had she cried than she started laughing').
j: 泣いたかと思うと、すぐ笑い出した。
e: No sooner had she cried than she started laughing.

gloss: not to the extent of / not as much as
pat: Plain form + ほどではない
x: 〜ほどではない is a negation of 〜ほど, expressing that something is 'not to the extent' of X — downplaying a comparison. Often used to moderate a previous statement: 'yes, but not that much'. Neutral / formal register.
notes: Moderating negation — 'not quite as much as X'.
Common to hedge: 痛いけど、救急車を呼ぶほどではない.
j: 痛いけど、病院に行くほどではない。
e: It hurts, but not to the extent of going to the hospital.

gloss: appears / seems (evidence-based, formal)
x: ようだ expresses an inference the speaker is making based on available evidence — 'it appears that', 'it seems that'. It is more formal and more tentative than みたい (its casual equivalent). It is also used for similes ('like X') and has a highly productive adverbial form ように ('in a way such that').
notes: Note the different connectors: な for na-adjectives, の for nouns — NOT だ.
Also used for similes: 彼は子供のようだ ('he is like a child').
j: 誰もいないようだ。
e: It seems nobody is here.

gloss: during / while (a period within which something happens)
pat: V 〜ている / noun-の / adj + 間 or 間に
x: 〜間 and 〜間に both express temporal 'during / while', but differ in scope: 〜間 (without に) covers the whole duration and is used with continuous main-clause actions that also span the whole period. 〜間に (with に) marks a point or sub-interval within the period, and is used for one-off events that happen during it. Subjects in the main clause and the 間 clause can differ.
notes: 〜間 (whole period): 私が日本にいる間、ずっと雨が降っていた.
〜間に (sub-interval): 私が寝ている間に、彼が来た.
j: 私が留守の間に誰か来ましたか。
e: Did someone come while I was out?

gloss: just (now) did / just about to do / in the middle of doing
x: ところ combined with different verb forms expresses the aspectual 'point of doing' an action: Vる + ところ = 'just about to', V 〜ている + ところ = 'in the middle of', Vた + ところ = 'just did (right now)'. Unlike 〜たばかり (subjective recency), 〜たところ refers to the immediate, clock-objective moment.
notes: Objectively 'just now' — typically within minutes of speaking.
Contrast with 〜たばかり, which is speaker-subjective and can span hours to days.
j: 今、駅に着いたところです。
e: I just arrived at the station (right now).

gloss: so that / in order to (non-volitional goal)
pat: V plain non-past (potential / intransitive / ない-form) + ように
x: ように as a purpose marker is used when the goal is a state or non-volitional outcome — typically with potential verbs (聞こえるように 'so one can hear'), intransitive verbs (雨が降らないように 'so the rain doesn't'), or the negative ない-form (忘れないように 'so I don't forget'). Contrast with ために, which is used for volitional main-clause actions.
notes: The subject of the ように clause may differ from the main clause.
Contrast with ために: ために is used when the main clause subject intentionally acts toward a goal they can control; ように is used when the goal is non-volitional or a state change.
j: よく聞こえるように大きい声で話してください。
e: Please speak loudly so (we) can hear well.

gloss: thanks to / because of (with explicit positive or negative attribution)
pat: V plain / noun-の + おかげで (positive) or せいで (negative)
x: おかげで and せいで both attribute a result to a cause, but with opposite polarity: おかげで ('thanks to') is used for positive outcomes, while せいで ('because of / at the fault of') is used for negative outcomes. They are structural twins — same connection patterns, opposite valence — and are typically taught as a pair.
notes: おかげで: positive outcomes only — thanks to (someone's help / a fortunate circumstance).
せいで: negative outcomes only — because of (someone's fault / an unfortunate circumstance).
j: あなたのおかげで合格できました。
e: Thanks to you, I was able to pass.

gloss: every time / whenever
pat: V plain non-past / noun-の + たびに
x: たびに attaches to a verb or noun phrase to express 'every time X happens, Y also happens'. It implies repetition with a consistent association — each occurrence of the たびに clause triggers the main clause. More emphatic and pattern-asserting than simply using 〜ときに ('when').
notes: Always uses the non-past form of the verb, even when describing repeated past events.
Main clause can be past, present, or future — the たびに clause stays non-past.
j: 彼に会うたびに、昔を思い出す。
e: Every time I see him, I remember the past.

gloss: whether or not
pat: Plain form (or noun / na-adj root) + かどうか
x: かどうか embeds a yes/no question inside another clause — 'whether ___ or not'. It attaches to a plain-form predicate. Crucially, the だ copula is dropped before かどうか for nouns and na-adjectives (学生かどうか, NOT 学生だかどうか). Contrast with embedded wh-questions (誰が来るか), which use か alone without どうか.
notes: Drop だ before かどうか for nouns and na-adjectives — this is a common error point.
For wh-questions (not yes/no), use か alone: 誰が来るか分からない ('I don't know who is coming').
j: 彼が来るかどうか分からない。
e: I don't know whether he'll come or not.

gloss: should / ought to (moral or social obligation)
x: べきだ expresses a moral or social 'should' — a normative claim that something ought to be done. It is stronger than 〜たほうがいい (suggestion / advice) and more abstract than 〜なければならない (concrete necessity). Often used in formal writing, opinion pieces, and moral advice. The negative form べきではない / べきじゃない means 'shouldn't'.
notes: Register: formal to neutral; appropriate in writing and formal speech, but also usable in personal advice.
Past form べきだった expresses regret or hindsight: そうするべきだった ('I should have done that').
j: 学生は勉強すべきだ。
e: Students should study.

gloss: even (emphatic, minimal case)
pat: Noun + さえ (+ negative or extreme statement)
x: さえ is an emphatic particle meaning 'even' — it highlights a minimal or unexpected case to make a point, often 'if even X (which is basic/minimal), then surely Y'. Commonly paired with conditional constructions (さえ〜ば 'if only X') or with negative statements to express surprise or disbelief ('even X doesn't Y'). More emphatic than でも in this sense.
notes: Emphasizes a minimal or unexpected case: 子供さえ知っている ('even a child knows').
〜さえ〜ば (sufficient condition): お金さえあれば ('if only I had money').
j: 子供さえ知っている。
e: Even a child knows.

gloss: as long as / to the extent that / as far as
pat: V plain / i-adj / noun + である + 限り
x: 〜限り has several related senses: (1) 'as long as' (as a condition continues) — V plain non-past + 限り; (2) 'to the extent that / as far as' (limit of knowledge or ability) — 知っている限り ('as far as I know'); (3) 'as long as X is the case' (condition on a state). A versatile marker for expressing scope or limit.
notes: V ない + 限り = 'unless' — 勉強しない限り、合格できない ('unless you study, you can't pass').
The negative variant 〜ない限り is very common for 'unless' constructions.
j: 生きている限り、希望はある。
e: As long as you're alive, there's hope.

gloss: to pretend to / act as if
x: 〜ふりをする expresses that the subject pretends to be or do something they actually are not or did not. ふり literally means 'appearance / pretense'. Commonly used in social situations where someone puts on a facade. The construction works with all predicate types: verbs, adjectives, and nouns (with の).
notes: ふり means 'pretense / appearance' and is often left in kana.
For na-adj and nouns, use the attributive form (な / の) before ふり.
j: 寝たふりをした。
e: I pretended to be asleep.

gloss: it's not (necessarily) that / it doesn't mean that
pat: Plain form + わけではない
x: 〜わけではない softens a negative — 'it's not that I don't X' or 'that doesn't mean X'. It hedges an implication that the speaker wants to deny without outright rejecting the broader topic. Common in explanations when correcting a listener's assumption: 'it's not like I hate it, it's just that...'. The casual contracted form is わけじゃない.
notes: Hedges a negation — 'not necessarily' rather than an outright 'no'.
Casual contraction: わけじゃない.
j: 嫌いなわけじゃないけど、今日は食べたくない。
e: It's not that I dislike it, I just don't feel like eating it today.

gloss: even if / even assuming / even for
x: 〜にしても is a concessive marker meaning 'even if / even assuming X' or 'even for (someone like) X'. It concedes a hypothetical or evaluative position and presents a main-clause observation regardless. Common in the fixed phrase どちらにしても / いずれにしても ('in any case / either way'). Also used to acknowledge an extreme example: 子供にしても、分かる ('even for a child, it's understandable').
notes: Concessive — 'even if' in a more formal / literary register than 〜ても.
Fixed phrase: どちらにしても / いずれにしても ('in any case / either way').
j: 失敗するにしても、挑戦するべきだ。
e: Even if you fail, you should try.

gloss: not necessarily / not always
pat: Plain form + とは限らない
x: 〜とは限らない expresses that a general statement has exceptions — 'X is not necessarily true' or 'not always X'. It hedges a generalization by saying it doesn't hold in every case. Often contrasts with a listener's assumption: 'you might think X, but it's not always the case'. Related in nuance to わけではない but more specifically about generalizations and exceptions.
notes: Hedges a generalization — common in discussions, advice, and corrections.
Often preceded by 必ずしも ('not necessarily', redundant but common): 必ずしも〜とは限らない.
j: 高いものがいいとは限らない。
e: Expensive things are not necessarily good.

gloss: toward / against / in contrast to
x: 〜に対して has two related senses: (1) 'toward / against' — marking the object of an attitude, action, or emotion directed at someone or something (親に対して失礼 'rude toward parents'); (2) 'in contrast to' — drawing an explicit contrast between two items (兄は静かなのに対して、弟はうるさい 'the older brother is quiet, whereas the younger one is loud'). The attributive form に対する / に対しての is productive.
notes: Directional sense: marks the target of an action, emotion, or attitude.
Contrast sense: requires のに before 対して when contrasting clauses.
j: 親に対して、失礼な態度を取ってはいけない。
e: You mustn't take a disrespectful attitude toward your parents.

gloss: together with / as X happens
pat: Noun / V plain + とともに
x: 〜とともに has two related senses: (1) 'together with' — noun + とともに, more formal than 〜と一緒に; (2) 'as X happens / simultaneously' — expressing parallel events or a relationship of co-occurrence. Literary / formal register. Can attach to noun, noun + する verb, or plain-form clause.
notes: Formal variant of 〜と一緒に for accompaniment.
Co-occurrence sense: 季節が変わるとともに、服装も変えた ('as the season changed, I changed my clothes').
j: 家族とともに新年を迎えた。
e: I welcomed the new year together with my family.

gloss: since last doing X, (haven't done Y) / only doing X and no more
x: 〜たきり expresses that after doing X, nothing further has been done — often with a negative continuation clause. It implies an interruption or a state that has persisted since the past event. Common for describing situations that have not changed since a specific past moment. Distinct from the simple きり (exclusivity).
notes: Usually followed by a negative: 〜たきり、〜ていない ('since doing X, haven't done Y').
Implies the state has persisted unchanged since the past event.
j: 昨日家を出たきり、まだ帰ってこない。
e: He left the house yesterday and still hasn't come back.

gloss: precisely because / being X, all the more
x: 〜だけに expresses a causal emphasis — 'precisely because X' or 'being X, (the consequence is) all the more (strong)'. It builds on だけ ('only / extent') but in a causal direction, implying that the degree of X corresponds to or amplifies the main clause's outcome. Often used to emphasize natural correspondence or heightened reactions.
notes: Causal and proportional — 'X being the case, Y is correspondingly so'.
Often with expected outcomes that are amplified by the cause: プロだけに上手だ ('being a pro, he's all the more skilled').
j: プロだけに、演奏が素晴らしい。
e: Being a pro, his performance is all the more splendid.

gloss: as one would expect from / fittingly
x: 〜だけあって expresses that the main-clause quality is 'fittingly' or 'as you would expect from' the characteristic described in the だけあって clause — 'being X, of course Y'. Positive evaluative nuance: the speaker endorses the main-clause claim as natural given the premise. Often used to compliment skills, qualities, or training.
notes: Positive evaluative — the consequence is praiseworthy / expected given the premise.
Contrast with だけに (neutral proportionality) — だけあって is endorsing.
j: 10年練習しただけあって、演奏が見事だ。
e: Having practiced for 10 years, his performance is splendid.

gloss: merely because / just because (often with negative outcome)
x: 〜ばかりに expresses that a minor or specific cause led to an (usually undesirable) consequence — 'merely because X, Y (unfortunately)'. Often used in regret or complaint contexts, emphasizing that the outcome stems from a single triggering cause. Distinct from 〜ばかり (only / nothing but).
notes: Typically negative outcomes — regret about a trigger that led to an unwanted result.
Distinct from 〜ばかり (exclusivity) and 〜たばかり (recent action).
j: 急いでいたばかりに、大切なものを忘れた。
e: Merely because I was in a hurry, I forgot something important.

gloss: not only X but also Y
x: 〜ばかりか is an additive construction meaning 'not only X, but also Y'. The Y clause usually extends the X claim, often to a more surprising or emphatic level. More formal than the casual 〜だけでなく. Common in emphatic or praiseworthy / critical descriptions. The shorter variant 〜どころか has a related but distinct use (far from X, actually Y).
notes: Additive: the Y clause adds to or intensifies the X clause.
More formal than 〜だけでなく (everyday 'not only').
j: 彼は英語ばかりか、フランス語も話せる。
